This forms a closed-loop system where each trial generates a feedback signal, which is then processed into a structured reflection and stored in memory. The process is defined mathematically as r_t = M_e(τ_t), sr_t = M_sr({τ_t, r_t}, mem), and mem ← mem ∪ {sr_t}, with |mem| ≤ Ω. The bounded nature of memory ensures computational tractability while preserving critical learning history. In GSE, this translates to a dynamic policy update mechanism where past failures inform future actions. For GSI, it offers a principled way to incorporate uncertainty quantification through reflective confidence intervals derived from repeated self-assessments.
